40% of the curve trading fee, paid to the token's creator.
Same as Fees: the full trading fee is paid by traders.
1% trading fee on RadarDEX Reflection-launch pools, always denominated in USDC regardless of the pool's own quote asset, read from each fee distribution event.
None. RadarDEX takes no cut of Reflection-launch fees; the entire 1% goes to the launched token's holders and its deployer.
None, for the same reason as Revenue.
The full 1% trading fee: 50% streamed to the launched token's holders pro-rata by balance, 50% to the deployer.
The full swap fee on every ubi.fun trade: the creator and protocol legs from FeeEscrow, plus the USDC-denominated half of referral payouts.
The team's 15% share of the total swap fee, confirmed on-chain against a real PlatformFeeSplitter distribution.
The creator's fee share, the 24% daily USDC holder-pool dividend, and the USDC-denominated half of referral payouts.

The fee a V5 or V6 launch pool charges on each trade, taken by that launch's hook inside the swap itself and read from the hook's own event, so the rate is never assumed here. It is 1% at regime; an anti-sniper launch charges more on buys during its opening window, on a curve that decays over the first blocks - 95%, then 70%, 40% and 10% - before settling at the same 1%, while sells in that window pay the regime rate. The fee is taken in either the launched token or its quote asset, whichever side the trader paid in. Both generations are read: V6 only took over new launches, it did not stop V5's existing pools from trading. V1-V4 legacy launches (pre-hook, plain Uniswap v3 with a per-launch lock contract) are not covered.

The protocol's share of each fee, which is a split of the fee and not a rate on the trade: it keeps 50% under the default split, 30% when the launch opted into Holder Rewards, and 10% of any fee taken during a launch's opening window, which has its own fixed split. All three are set by the contract and not adjustable after launch.

Everything not kept by the protocol: the creator's share, the remainder streamed to the launched token's own holders via the Reward Vault on Holder-Rewards launches, and - on fees taken during the opening window - the 80% earmarked to the launch's Treasury Reserve, which buys the launched token back to burn it.
Every leg of aka.fun's per-trade fee distribution: platform, creator/RWA-treasury, referral, and community drop, in USDC.
The platform's share: 20% of the fee with a referral, or 35% without one (the forfeited referral cut goes to the platform).
The creator/RWA-treasury share, the community drop share, and the referral payout when present.

Curve mode: flat 1% fee on every bonding-curve buy/sell, read from each trade's own gross USDC amount. Post-graduation: 1% swap fee on CircleWarp's own WarpDex pools (a custom Uniswap V2 fork), taken from whichever side of the swap is the input token. Token creation itself is free (no launch fee).
Curve mode: 50% of the curve trading fee. Post-graduation: 30% of the WarpDex pool swap fee.

Curve mode: 50% of the curve trading fee, paid to the token's creator. Post-graduation: 30% of the pool swap fee to the creator, plus the 40% LP share that stays in the pool as reserve growth (the LP position itself is burned at graduation, so this permanently compounds into the pool rather than paying out to a live LP holder).
Trading fees paid by traders on every Ascend launch-pool trade.
Trading fees charged by the Ascend launchpad on every launch-pool trade, counted when they are settled to each coin's creator escrow (normally within an hour of the trade).
The part of trading fees sent to the Ascend protocol splitter, plus the part used by the launchpad's standing bids to buy launched coins into protocol treasuries.

The protocol splitter's team, strategic KNTQ, stakers and strategic HYPE legs, plus standing-bid buys of launched coins into protocol treasuries. The stakers leg is held in a protocol treasury while staking is not live.
The part of trading fees paid to coin creators (including the share held in escrow until a coin graduates), to builders who brought the launch, and to buybacks of the launched coin.
The 28.8% of the protocol splitter's share set aside to burn KNTQ.
1% swap fee on every trade of a launched token, creator-set buy/sell taxes on tax tokens, and the 1 USDC fee per token launch.
25% of swap fees plus token creation fees, kept by the protocol.
Same as Revenue; ARK has no token, so nothing goes to holders.
75% of swap fees plus all token taxes, paid to token creators.

The full USDC mint-settlement price paid by miners for every ArcLotls organism, read from the three downstream shares (rent, treasury, buyback) the mint payment is split into on-chain, which always sum to 100% of the mint price. Excludes the LOTL opening-trade tax (a one-time anti-snipe launch mechanic) and any undocumented trading-fee revenue not yet observed on-chain.
Mint fees minus the share paid out as rent to NFT holders: the treasury share plus the share earmarked for the LOTL buyback-and-burn reserve.
The treasury share of every mint (25% as observed on-chain).
The rent share of every mint (60% as observed on-chain), paid out to NFT holders weighted by organism stage. Accrued when funded, not when claimed.
The share of every mint earmarked for buying LOTL back and burning it (15% as observed on-chain), measured at the fee source (when USDC lands in the buyback reserve) rather than at execution.
1% swap fee charged by Tsunami's fee hook on every swap (buy and sell alike)

The protocol's share of the swap fee: 100% before the creator-fee hook upgrade, then the documented default share (70% original factory, 99% second factory) after - a curve can be configured with a different split
Same as Revenue: all protocol-side fees go to the Tsunami treasury, there is no token holder distribution
The token creator's documented default share of the swap fee (30% original factory, 1% second factory) once the creator-fee hook was live - a curve can be configured with a different split
Total swap fee (LP + protocol) from each trade's Swap event.
Protocol's cut of the swap fee, via v4-core's protocol-fee switch (0% until a pool is stamped, then up to 0.1% each direction).
Same as Revenue - Calamari has no token or holder distribution.
Remainder of the swap fee, paid to LPs.
Swap fees (currently 1% of the swap) and optional creator tax charged by the Wonk Fun hook on every swap, before and after graduation, there is no launch fee
protocolFeeShareBps of the swap fees sent to the Wonk Fun treasury, currently 1%
All revenue goes to the Wonk Fun treasury, there is no token holder distribution
Swap fees paid by traders, plus bribes paid to the protocol to attract AERO Rewards to pools.
Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity, the protocol share of fee-earning liquidity fees and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.
Swap fees kept by fee-earning liquidity providers, and all fees of the original Aero Lite pools on Arc, which have no gauges.
Trade fees on every buy/sell of Dynamito tokens (1-3% tier plus the anti-snipe surcharge in the first 5 seconds) and the 3% blast-off fee at graduation.
40% of trade fees plus 50% of blast-off fees, kept by Dynamito.

Same as Revenue (40% of trade fees plus 50% of blast-off fees): all of it is kept by the Dynamito treasury. No token holder distribution yet; when the $TNT buyback programme starts, its share will be reported as HoldersRevenue.
40% of trade fees and 50% of blast-off fees paid to creators, plus the 20% of trade fees paid to the Meteora protocol.
Same as fees, paid by traders.

Trading fees collected by vibes.fun: the 1% platform fee on every trade against the Raydium LaunchLab bonding curves it configures, and, once a coin graduates, the quote-side trading fees of its permanently locked liquidity, harvested with the Fee Key vibes.fun holds. Raydium's own protocol fee is excluded. Amounts are in each pool's quote token.
30% of fees: the share vibes.fun keeps, split between its treasury and $VIBES buyback and burn.
15% of fees, sent to the vibes.fun treasury (Squads multisig).
70% of fees, paid to the holders of the coin that generated them, or to its creator when the creator chose creator fees.
15% of fees, used to buy back and burn $VIBES.
All REP369 transaction tax paid by users. The adapter reads fee-component settings from the REP369 contract and applies on-chain fee-update events in chronological order.
REP369 tax allocated to REP holder rewards plus the sell-side burn allocation. Automatic liquidity is treated as supply-side revenue.
No separate protocol treasury fee is present in the current REP369 fee configuration.
The portion of REP369 transaction tax allocated to automatic liquidity.
REP rewards plus the REP369 sell-side burn allocation.
Same as Fees: every fee is paid by traders on buys and sells.

All trading fees settled into FociFeeEscrow during the day (curve fees, creator tax, converted post-graduation hook fees, curve referral fees), plus hook referral fees claimed that day. Recognised when swept by the keeper, not when traded.
Protocol fee recipient's share plus the share paid to holder-reward distributors.
Escrow credits to the protocol fee recipient (the protocol's frozen share of each launch's trading fee).
Escrow credits to creators (their fee share and the creator tax) and to referrers, plus hook referral claims.
Escrow credits to FociRewardsDistributor contracts — launches that elected to pay their creator share to token holders.

LP fees and gauge rewards earned by the TickerSpring vaults during the UTC day, including amounts not yet collected. V7 vaults: the change in cumulative harvested plus pending native-token fees from saved on-chain observations. Vaults that replaced V7 (listed by https://api.tickerspring.com/v1/merged/vaults): the trading fees and gauge rewards (UP on Up, RAM on Ramses) their Harvest events collected plus the change in uncollected position fees and unclaimed rewards, read on-chain at the day's first and last blocks. Excludes principal, stock-price returns, retired vaults and lending.
Earned vault LP fees and gauge rewards allocated to operations (10%) and the SPRING buyback reserve (20%), subject to raw-token rounding.
The operations allocation (10%) of earned vault LP fees and gauge rewards.
Earned LP fees and gauge rewards retained for vault depositors after protocol allocations (approximately 70%).
The allocation of earned vault LP fees and gauge rewards reserved to buy and permanently burn SPRING (20%), measured when they accrue rather than when the buyback executes.

The tax ArgusPad's per-launch hook charges on every buy and sell, the trading fee each launch's pool charges (on Portals 3-7 the 1% pool fee earned by the permanently locked launch position; on Portal 8 a 1% base fee the hook charges in the quote asset in its place), and the extra tax charged on buys in a launch's first seconds. Counted in the asset the fee is charged in, at the moment it is charged, so the protocol's later sale of the launched tokens it was paid is not counted a second time. Fees charged in the launched token itself (Portals 3-7 only; Portal 8 takes every fee in the quote asset) are reported in that token's own units and are priced only if DefiLlama has a price for it; it has none for these tokens today, because a launched token's only market is the pool ArgusPad seeded, and pricing it there overstates by about 40% against what ArgusPad's own sales of them actually realise.

The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.

The rest of the fees, which leave the protocol divided at the weights each launch fixed at creation: the token creator's share, the dividends paid to holders of that launched token, the share added back into the launch's permanently locked liquidity, the share used to buy and burn the launched token, and on Portal 8 the share used to buy the launched token and lock it permanently.
The 1.00% protocol trading fee paid on DaWabLauncher bonding-curve buys and sells, read directly from each trade event. DaWabLauncher charges no separate market-creation or graduation fee.
All DaWabLauncher bonding-curve trading fees are retained as protocol revenue.
All DaWabLauncher bonding-curve trading fees are allocated to the protocol.
Crate spend net of instant-sell buyback payouts (Orderbook trades signed by the Treasury). Can be negative on heavy-buyback days.
Treasury share of each open (crate price minus Pot contribution, plus network fee) minus buyback payouts. Gross of off-chain card fulfillment (every crate delivers a physical graded card).
Treasury share of each open (crate price minus Pot contribution, plus network fee) minus buyback payouts.
The Pot contribution of each open: a fixed bps of the crate price funding the community jackpot paid back to players.
Gross realized Vault yield above the high-water mark plus crystallized management fees. Yield is inferred by grossing up newly crystallized performance fees at each Vault's on-chain fee rate.
Management and performance fee shares crystallized by MoneyFi, valued at the period-end net share price.
Crystallized management and performance fees allocated to MoneyFi.
The remainder of crystallized gross performance yield allocated to Vault depositors after MoneyFi's performance fee.

1% base fee on every bonding-curve buy and sell, plus the creator's optional tax, plus the anti-snipe tax charged in the first 3 seconds of a launch, plus a flat launch fee per token (read live from each chain's factory), plus 2% of the raise taken when a curve graduates to Uniswap v4.
The protocol's share of the base curve fee (10% normally, 30% once a chain is past its first 100 launches), half of the anti-snipe tax, all launch fees, and the full 2% graduation fee.
The launch creator's share of the base curve fee (90% for the first 100 launches on a chain, 70% after), their full optional creator tax, and half of the anti-snipe tax charged on their token.
Open fees and profit fees paid by traders.
Flat 0.5 USDG open fee per order unless refunded, plus a 5% fee on settled trader profits. Trader losses go to the treasury that backs payouts and are not counted as fees.
Fees minus the builder carve; there are no liquidity providers.
Revenue minus holders revenue.
Builder carve paid to the frontend that placed the order, out of the operations share.
MOG bought back and burned by the buyback wallet, valued at the MOG price. 70% of profit fees accrue to that wallet; only the MOG it burns is counted.
1 USDC create fee, 1% bonding-curve trade fee, and 0.25% Load router fee on Instant/graduated swaps.

Protocol share: all create fees plus 20% of the 1% curve fee (0.20% of curve volume) plus Load router platform fees. The 5% launch-referrer cut of the create fee is included here because it is not emitted on-chain.
All create fees plus 20% of the 1% curve fee (0.20% of curve volume) plus Load router platform fees. The 5% launch-referrer cut of the create fee is included here because it is not emitted on-chain.
80% of the 1% curve fee to creators, plus trader-referral share of the 0.25% router fee.

The Civilization anti-snipe pad snipe tax on Nightshades faction curve buys (PadTaxCollected — 50% next-night boost pot / 10% faction pool / 13.33% StockBooster / 13.33% protocol / 13.34% game creator, WETH); the sunrise reopen snipe tax levied by the game hook on hooked v4 pool trades after each night (SnipeTaxCollected, same five-way split); the 1% LP fee on every user swap in the hooked faction pools (100% protocol-owned game liquidity — the vault is the pools' only permitted LP); and Nightshades faction NFT royalties (ERC-2981 10% of secondary sales) as flushed from the immutable FactionRoyaltySplitter (75% game vault survivor liquidity / 25% team).
The 13.33% protocol treasury leg of the pad + sunrise reopen snipe taxes, and the 1% LP fee accruing to the protocol-owned faction pool liquidity.
13.33% of the pad + sunrise reopen snipe taxes → protocol treasury; the faction pools' 1% LP fee → the vault's protocol-owned game liquidity position (compounds into game LP, not distributed).
Pad + sunrise reopen tax legs to the next-night boost pot (50%), the faction's own locked pool (10%), StockBooster (13.33%) and the game creator (13.34%), plus both legs of the flushed NFT royalties.
Gross Uniswap V3 pool fees collected by every registry-listed Smart LP (Volatility Farming) vault (FeesCollected fees0/fees1).
The $STONKBROKER-buyback half of the 10% performance fee.
90% of vault pool fees auto-compounded to depositors plus the StockBooster Clock In dividend half of the 10% performance fee.

ETH fees on NFT AMM trades + NFT-backed loans; $STONKBROKER broker activation/upgrade fees; Stonk Interns mint fees (ETH leg, $STONKBROKER leg, $1 promotion fee) and intern activation fees; and the Relay swap-desk 1% app fee (Base USDC forwarded to StockBooster).

30% of NFTFi ETH fees, the full $STONKBROKER activation fee (burn + protocol), and the Stonk Interns protocol share (75% of the ETH mint leg, 100% of the STONK leg and promotion fee, the full intern activation fee).
30% of NFTFi ETH fees → ProtocolFeeSink; protocol half of $STONKBROKER activation fees; Stonk Interns treasury legs and the protocol half of intern activation fees.
70% of NFTFi ETH fees → StockBooster stock dividends; 25% of the Stonk Interns mint ETH leg → intern Clock In payroll; Relay swap-desk 1% app fees forwarded to StockBooster.
Half of the $STONKBROKER broker and intern activation/upgrade fees burned.
Broker Box gachapon 10% edge (EdgeSkimmed) + the 5% sell-back spread retained in the machine bankroll + the Certificate Counter flat $2 fee.
Broker Box protocol accrual (5% of ticket) + sell-back spread + the treasury half of the Certificate Counter fee.
Broker Box protocol accrual + sell-back bankroll spread + the treasury half of the Certificate Counter fee.
Broker Box creator + booster edge (5% of ticket on official machines) → StockBooster Clock In stock drops, plus the StockBooster half of the Certificate Counter fee.

Safe Launch / Stonklauncher snipe tax on window buys and sells across all pad generations (16.5% creator / 16.5% protocol / 50% locked-LP or ICO Bonus / 17% StockBooster + Clock In Card referrers); the anti-snipe fair-launch snipe tax (time-decay tax on launch-curve buys, 90% StockBooster / 10% launch dev); and StonkCurvePool 1% trade fees (33/33/33 waterfall).
The 16.5% protocol leg of the Safe Launch / Stonklauncher snipe tax and 33.34% of bonding-curve trade fees.
16.5% of the Safe Launch / Stonklauncher snipe tax → protocol accrual; 33.34% of bonding-curve trade fees → protocol.

Safe Launch tax legs to the launch creator (16.5%), StockBooster + Clock In Card referrers (17%), and the permanently locked LP reserve / ICO Bonus (50%); 90% of the anti-snipe launch tax → StockBooster dividends and 10% → launch dev; bonding-curve creator (33.33%) + StonkBrokers Directed Clock In / pot (33.33%).

Token creation, bonding-curve trading (including any launch-window surcharge), Genius hook trading and paid Alpha promotion fees. Fees accrue at launch/trade/promotion; settlements are excluded. Meme-denominated hook fees use the same swap’s quote/meme execution-price ratio, rounded down to quote base units.

The Genius platform share of trading fees under each launch’s immutable policy, plus separately labeled creation and Alpha promotion fees. The creator-selected destination allocation (Foundation or creator), creator share and launched-meme buyback allocations are excluded.
The same protocol-retained portion as Revenue. Genius.fun has no protocol token receiving these fees.

Creator-selected destination allocations (Foundation or creator), creator shares and accrued funding for buybacks of individual launched meme tokens, calculated from immutable per-launch policies with contract integer rounding.

Every USDC a user pays the protocol: the 1% trade fee on the USDC side of each trade, on the bonding curve and in the graduated token's Uniswap v4 pool alike; the fee to create a token (1 USDC at deployment); the snipe tax on buys in a token's first 120 blocks; and the USDC left over once a graduating token's Uniswap v4 pool has been seeded.
The platform's share: 0.30% of a trade where the trader has a referrer bound on chain and 0.50% where they do not, plus all launch fees, all snipe tax and the graduation dust.

Same as Revenue (0.30% of a trade where the trader has a referrer bound on chain and 0.50% where they do not, plus all launch fees, all snipe tax and the graduation dust). There is no protocol token, so nothing is distributed to holders.
0.50% of every trade to the token's creator and 0.20% to the trader's referrer, both claimable from the FeeManager.
Swap fees paid by traders of LIFT v1 tokens and launch fees paid by token deployers.

The 1% Uniswap V3 LP fee earned by every locked LIFT v1 launch position, counted in the pool's quote asset when the position's fees are harvested (token-side fees burned by the first-generation locker are excluded), plus the flat fee paid for every token launch.
The LIFT treasury share of harvested swap fees plus all launch fees.
The token creator share of harvested swap fees, fixed per position when it is created.
No fees are distributed to holders of a protocol token.
Swap fees paid by traders of LIFT v2 tokens and launch fees paid by token deployers.

Fees the LIFT v2 hook takes in the pool's quote asset (USDC or EURC) on every swap of a LIFT v2 token: the base fee, including the anti-snipe surcharge in a launch's first blocks, plus the fee each creator sets for buys and sells. Counted when the swap happens, plus the flat fee paid for every token launch.
The LIFT treasury share of the base fee plus all launch fees. LIFT takes no share of the creator swap fee.

Everything else goes to the creator side of each launch: the rest of the base fee and the whole creator swap fee, split by the launch's fixed settings between the creator, buyback and burn of the launched token, dividends to holders of the launched token, and liquidity added to the launch's locked pool.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perpetual trades placed through WatchCrypto; excludes Hyperliquid exchange trading fees.
Builder code fees collected by WatchCrypto from Hyperliquid perpetual trades.
Same as Fees; every fee is paid by the trader.

All swap fees paid by traders on Arctide pools, in USDC: the pool's LP fee, its protocol fee (set by the token creator) and Arctide's fixed 0.25% treasury fee, read from the Router's SwapExecuted events.
Arctide's 0.25% treasury fee on every swap, plus the protocol fees of the pools whose protocol recipient is Arctide itself (the $TIDE and $DUCK pools).
30% of Revenue, retained by Arctide.
LP fees credited to liquidity providers, plus protocol fees paid to token creators' chosen addresses.
70% of Revenue, used to buy back and burn $TIDE.
Pool swap fees paid by traders (pool-level swapFee × amount in).
Protocol share of swap fees (ProtocolFeesCollector / ProtocolFeeController percentage read live from kiltr.net/api/fees).
Protocol share of swap fees, using the v2 or v3 percentage from kiltr.net/api/fees.
Swap fees remaining with liquidity providers (Fees − Revenue).
Fees paid directly by Denaria users to Denaria: the GMX UI fee and the flat service fee. Affiliate rewards are excluded because they are a rebate out of the fee the trader pays to GMX.

Fees collected by Denaria: the GMX UI fee charged on Denaria orders, the affiliate reward earned by the DENARIA referral code on GMX position fees, and the flat per-operation service fee paid to the Denaria fee wallet. GMX position, borrowing and funding fees are not Denaria fees and are counted under GMX V2 Perps.
All Denaria fees (GMX UI fees, affiliate rewards, service fees) are revenue.
All revenue (GMX UI fees, affiliate rewards, service fees) accrues to the Denaria fee wallets.
None: Denaria has no liquidity providers of its own on GMX.
None: Denaria has no token.
The 9.99% fee charged in the quote token on every desk fill (InternExchange FeeRouted toDesk + toEngine + toTreasury).
The 9% treasury share of the fee.
The 66% share paid to the desk whose staked liquidity filled the trade plus the 25% share routed to the Stonk Interns Clock In engine as dividends to activated intern NFT holders.
Token creation fees paid in STRK and extra trading fees charged by the original Launchy router.
Creation fees plus Launchy's original router fee share. Launchy-created Ekubo pool fees are reported separately under Launchy Pools.
All Launchy revenue is directed to the platform treasury.
Creator fees from the original Launchy router.
Swap fees generated in Launchy-created Ekubo pools. These fees are also reported by Ekubo.
Launchy's 30% share of guarded-pool swap fees. The original pool has no Launchy LP share.
Launchy's share of guarded-pool fees allocated to its treasury.
Creator and Ekubo shares of Launchy-created pool swap fees.

What users pay to cross the bridge. The asset's controller on Arc charges the same rate in both directions - on the way in it mints the fee to the protocol and the rest to the user, on the way out it burns the gross and re-mints the fee - and an optional fast-lane router charges its own cut on top for skipping the queue, on the origin chain when depositing and on Arc when redeeming. Anything charged on Arc is taken in the claim token (bCRCL, bGLD, bUSDT, bBTCB), which is a 1:1 claim on the asset held in custody and is therefore valued as that origin asset; a fast-lane deposit is charged on the origin chain instead, before the asset becomes a claim, so it is taken in the origin token directly. Either way the fee is denominated in the same four origin assets.
All the bridge fees and the fast-lane fees go to the protocol's treasury with nothing paid out of it.
None. The bridge has no liquidity providers - claim tokens are backed by custody reserves, not by a pool, so there is no supplier to pay.

Meow's own output fee (0.25% by default, lower for wallets holding the configured token), taken from each swap's output and emitted as FeeCollected. Fees charged by the underlying pools are not included.
All swap fees accrue to the Meow treasury.
All swap fees are retained by the Meow treasury.
No part of the fee goes to liquidity providers, integrators or referrers.
Same as Fees: every part is paid by users.
Creator tax on swaps of coins launched through Kicker pots (floor, launcher, buyback and platform parts) plus the 0.5% fee on pot deposits, in the pot's core asset.

The platform shares (10% of taxes on coins launched with terms and the platform part of deposit fees) plus the core that pots spend buying and burning KICKER (Burn events with KICKER as the burned token). Creator tax onto pot floors is not revenue.
The platform shares, received by KickerBuyer. KickerBuyer later spends them on KICKER buybacks and burns; that spend is not counted again.

Creator tax collected onto pot floors (accrues to pot depositors), launcher shares and buyback shares with any target but KICKER of taxes on coins launched with terms, and pot creator / referrer parts of deposit fees.

Core that pots spend buying and burning KICKER, counted when the burn executes (Burn event, KICKER burned, tokens > 0), from the buyback share of taxes on coins launched with KICKER as their burn target. Pot shares (K) are redeemable vault shares, not a governance or value-accrual token, so floor accrual is not holders revenue.

Concentrated liquidity swap fees paid by traders. Each swap is charged on its input amount at the dynamic CLPool.fee() in effect for that swap (read from the state right before the swap's block; 3000 means 0.30%), net of any registered tx.origin discount.
Concentrated liquidity fees routed to veArchery voters through gauges, equal to HoldersRevenue.
Concentrated liquidity provider fees not routed to veArchery voters.

Fees from the GAS/USO pool that reach Gas (95% of the swap tax and of the LP fee; Doppler keeps the other 5%), plus what players pay to buy NFT cars (in $GAS) and to repair them (in USO). The 15-minute launch sniper tax on 2026-09-23 (forwarded to a team wallet during the launch tax decay) is not counted.
All car sales and repairs, plus the 25% of pool fees sent to the buybacks wallet.
The treasury's 20% of car sales and all car repairs.

Pool fees sent to the prize pool, which pays players in USO when they claim at gas stations (75% of pool fees since 2026-09-23 06:03 UTC, all of them before). The team sells the prize pool's $GAS into USO by hand.

Pool fees and car-sale shares sent to the buybacks wallet 0x18eD3E25Fb4786EA60021E2e9A2Da0A52602f503: 25% of pool fees, and 80% of car sales since 2026-09-23 05:59 UTC (paid in $GAS and held in that wallet). Buybacks are made by hand when the team decides and have not started yet. Before 2026-09-23 05:59 UTC the 80% car-sale share was burned.
Same as Fees: the router fee is paid entirely by the swapper.

Router fee taken on the input leg of every swap through TartSwapRouterV2 (TartSwapExecuted.feeAmount, 35 bps by default, per-account custom fees possible). Excludes PancakeSwap's LP fee on the forwarded swap.
Share of the swap fee that TartFeeDistributor routes to the treasury and reserve legs, per its on-chain split() at the end of the period.
Same as Revenue: the treasury and reserve swap fees are held by the protocol.
Share of the swap fee that TartFeeDistributor routes to the farm and staking reward legs, which are converted and streamed to LP and CREPE stakers.
1% (100 bps) app fee charged on swaps routed through Relay, collected in USDC. Reported per origin chain of the swap.
All app fees accrue to the Based protocol; there is no supply-side or holder share.
Identical to Revenue: the full app fee is kept by the protocol.

All stock- and launched-token-denominated swap charges in V1 and V2 V4 pools, including opening-period charges and caller incentives; all V2 bonding-curve trading fees and opening-window token burns; plus launch fees. Token charges are recorded in raw units and contribute to USD totals only when DefiLlama pricing supports them; missing prices leave USD coverage incomplete. Excludes strategy profits and buybacks, Uniswap LP fees, external routing fees, and Pons/$HEDGE taxes.

The designated protocol share of stock trading fees on the curve and in pools as they accrue, the creator share of launches made by the protocol recipient itself, plus launch fees; excludes royalties of other creators and launched-token strategy allocations.
The same protocol allocations as Revenue, including earned but unswept or unclaimed amounts.

Stock trading fees less the protocol allocations go to creators, strategies and sweep callers; all launched-token charges go to token burns and sweep callers, with no platform revenue. Token amounts require DefiLlama price coverage for USD inclusion.
Users pay all of the fees.

USDC creation fee paid by users to create an AI agent on Arc through the Fuci agent factory (1 USDC per agent at launch; read from each AgentCreated event), plus the fee on escrow jobs paid out to an agent (1% of the job at launch; read from each FuciEscrow Released event), plus Fuci Launch trading fees: the 1% Uniswap v4 LP fee on every swap in a launch pool and the snipe tax on early buys.
Creation fees, escrow fees and the Fuci Launch snipe tax (all sent to the Fuci treasury, a Safe multisig), plus Fuci Launch LP fees paid in $FUCI, which are all burned.
Creation fees, escrow fees and the Fuci Launch snipe tax, all sent to the Fuci treasury (a Safe multisig).
Fuci Launch LP fees paid in the launched token. They are burned too, which benefits that token's holders.
$FUCI burned by the Fuci launchpad's collectAndBurn, which collects each launch's LP fees and burns them, usually once a day.
2% performance fee on the realised profit of each copied position, charged only on profitable closes.
The 0.8% of realised profit kept by the protocol, measured directly as USDG transfers into the treasury.
The 1.2% of realised profit paid to the copied trader (leader), derived from the fixed fee split.

Swap fees paid by traders, taken from each Swap event's swapFeeAmount. The Vault charges the fee on the input token; it is booked on the same leg as the volume. When that leg is the output token (a non-core token sold for a core asset), the fee is converted at the trade's own rate, amountOut * swapFeeAmount / amountIn - no external price is used. The amount is exact; only its denomination changes. Because amountIn includes the fee itself and the trade's average rate is slightly worse than the pool's marginal rate, the converted fee reads low by about the pool's fee rate plus the trade's own price impact - a share of the fee, never of volume, and always in the under-counting direction.
The protocol's share of the swap fee, read per pool from the protocol fee controller.
Same as Revenue - the protocol's share of the swap fee goes to the protocol fee controller.
The rest of the swap fee: the part that stays in the pool for liquidity providers, plus the pool creator's share when a pool creator has set one.
Zero - no part of the fee is distributed to token holders today.
Interest paid by Alula borrowers plus operation fees on deposits, withdrawals, borrows, repayments and collateral moves.
The take rate on borrower interest (set per pool) plus operation fees, paid to the protocol and its insurance fund.
Borrower interest net of the take rate, earned by lenders.
Same as Fees: what the trader paid on each swap.

Two things the trader pays. The pool fee on each swap - two of these pools run Ellipse's market-hours hook and charge 1%, 2% or 3% depending on whether the underlying market is open or shut, so for those the rate is read from the swap itself rather than assumed, and the rest are fixed at creation. Plus Ellipse's own 0.5% on swaps routed through its front end, read from the event its fee collector emits when it is emptied, which reports what actually reached the treasury rather than what was sent.

Ellipse's 0.5% interface fee, kept in full. It is charged on every swap routed through its front end, which is a wider set than the pools whose volume is reported here, so it is not 0.5% of that volume and should not be read as a rate on it. It is dated when the collector is emptied rather than when each swap paid it; a keeper does that hourly.
The pool fee, which goes to the liquidity providers.
Acquisition fees net of quick-sell payouts, plus settlement fees, retained penalties and early crown exit fees.
Protocol's cut of fees after builder rewards, kept by the team or spent on burned FWA.
Protocol's cut of fees paid to the team.
Fees paid to NFT depositors, builder rewards, and the FWA rewards and caller incentive paid from buybacks.
FWA bought back with protocol fees and burned.

The 0.25% integrator fee HyperDex charges on every swap, bridge and basket order routed through LI.FI: the FeesForwarded leg paid to HyperDex in a transaction whose LI.FI event carries integrator "hyperdex" (Robinhood Chain and Solana: the integrator share of each transfer's fee from LI.FI's analytics API, in USD); HyperDex's leg of its client fee on Fynd swaps, from the TychoRouter FeesTaken event; and HyperDex's fee on RAVN, Velora, Hinkal and CoW swaps, at its fee rate on each completed swap in HyperDex's own swap record (https://hyperdex.app/api/defillama), at the swap's dollar amount when sent.
All of these fees go to HyperDex.
Same as Fees: these amounts originated from $HEDGE traders' swap charges.

Quote-asset fees and creator tax settled by Pons V2 on the $HEDGE/NVDA curve and its specific graduated pool. Uses the curve and hook sweep events, like the existing Pons V2 adapter; it does not count subsequent escrow claims or Safe transfers again.

The creatorAmount allocated to $HEDGE's fee recipient by its curve and graduated-pool sweeps. This combines the creator's share of Pons' standard fee and the creator tax; the event does not separate them. Classification of token tax as revenue is subject to DefiLlama review.
Pons' protocol allocation and any Pons buyback allocation from the same sweeps. These are not retained by $HEDGE.
Builder code fees paid by traders on free Floatout DEXes, on top of Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
Builder code fees collected by Floatout on free DEXes.
Same as Fees: all reported trading fees are paid directly by users.
All fees paid by traders in Synthra pools (each pool fee tier) and on Synthra Launch curves (the exact Trade fee).
Pool protocol fees, the protocol share of fees earned by launch positions locked at graduation, and the exact Launch protocol share.
Same as Revenue (Protocol share of fees earned by launch positions locked at graduation and Launch protocol share): all of it accrues to the Synthra treasury.
Pool LP fees except the protocol share of locked launch positions, creator shares of locked launch positions and of Launch fees, and the Launch fee share that funds buybacks of the launched token.
Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on perpetual trades executed through Synthra.
Hyperliquid builder code fees collected by Synthra from perpetual trades.
Application fees paid by users on successful Synthra router trades routed through Relay and LI.FI.
Application fees paid on successful Synthra router trades: Relay paidAppFees and LI.FI integrator fees. Trades whose fee could not be verified are excluded.
All router application fees are collected by Synthra.
All router application fees are collected by the Synthra fee recipient.
Same as Fees: every included amount is paid by a miner in a successful Boneyard mint.

The full native-USDC entry price accepted for every BoneYard NFT mint, read from Boneyard's Minted.price event. Excludes BONE genesis reserve, BONE emitted by burns, secondary royalties, and hook swap levies.

Mint fees less Charge paid to existing Skeletons. Before LP activation, the retained revenue is the project share plus protocol-owned liquidity bootstrap; after LP activation it is the project share plus BONE-buyback funding.

The project slice emitted by Hook.ProjectShareAdded plus the pre-LP bootstrap retained by Boneyard to seed its canonical protocol-owned liquidity. If seedLiquidity diverts bootstrap that cannot be paired with BONE into the Hook buyback reserve, that previously booked protocol revenue is reclassified out on BootstrapDivertedToBuyback. Hook-bound revenue is 100% of each of the first eight genesis mints and 35% of later mints.
Charge accrued to active Skeleton holders from mint #9 onward (65% under the deployed constant). Charge is measured when it accrues, not when a holder later claims or burns.

Native USDC allocated by Hook.BuybackAccrualAdded from post-LP mints for market-buying and burning BONE, plus any pre-LP bootstrap reclassified to that reserve by BootstrapDivertedToBuyback at liquidity seeding. It is counted when funded, not when the owner executes the capped buyback. BONE is the protocol's own value-accrual token.

Fees are tracked from the fee field in Swapped events, denominated in the input token. A swap is free unless its route beats the best single DEX by at least 0.1%, counted after gas; the fee is then at most 0.5% (0.05% between stablecoins; 0.15% on router v1).
All swap fees go to the Felynx treasury.

Commission paid by limit-order makers (2.5% on the Limit Orders hooks and 1% on the strategy hook, of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn) plus the Uniswap v4 LP fees earned by resting order liquidity, booked when an order is settled or partially filled at creation. Amounts in other tokens are valued on the USDG side at the order band's own execution price.
All commission (2.5% on the Limit Orders hooks and 1% on the strategy hook, of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.
LP fees earned by order liquidity, net of commission, credited to order makers.

Everything users pay through Packed: the flat 0.0004 ETH launch fee, the 1% fee on every trade on a Packed bonding curve (Robinhood Chain), the 1% LP fee of every Packed coin's Uniswap v4 pool (after graduation on Robinhood Chain, from launch on Ethereum), the creator tax a coin's creator sets at launch (0-5%, on curve trades and pool swaps), the anti-snipe charges of a coin's first seconds or first block, and the bids paid for seats in packs launched from deposits on Ethereum. All of it is paid by users: launch fees and bids by creators and pack members, the rest by traders. Pool fees are counted when they are collected from the position.
Packed's share: the launch fee in full, 25% of the 1% curve fee, 25% of the 1% pool fee, and half of every seat bid.
Revenue minus the ETH the fee wallet spends buying back $PACKD, which is moved to HoldersRevenue. Negative on days when a buyback spends more than that day's revenue.

The creator's 75% of the 1% curve and pool fees, the whole creator tax and anti-snipe charges, and the launcher's half of seat bids. For a reward coin the creator's share goes to the coin's holders instead.

ETH Packed spends buying back $PACKD, its own token, on the open market on Robinhood Chain; the coins bought are burned. Only the fee wallet's buys are counted: they are paid out of Packed's revenue above and moved out of ProtocolRevenue.
Fees users pay on the swaps Rhiva's zap program makes, charged on the SOL side of each swap.
The share of the swap fees Rhiva keeps, paid to its fee vault.
The share of the swap fees paid to the referrers set on the swap.
V2 swap fees paid by traders, taken from each pool's Fees events, which record the exact fee charged on each swap's input amount at the fee rate in effect for that swap.
V2 swap fees routed to veArchery voters through gauges, equal to HoldersRevenue.
V2 liquidity provider fees not routed to veArchery voters.

Fees accrued to the gauge's staked LP balance, from the pool's fee index accounting: change in claimable + balanceOf(gauge) * (index - supplyIndex[gauge]) / 1e18, plus fees the gauge claimed in the period.
Users pay the 0.05% swap fee.
0.05% fee that users pay on every swap made through World by Starra, settled in USDC.
All swap fees go to the protocol.
All swap fees go to the protocol treasury.
What players spend on Card Wall card pack pulls, net of refunds and of the $WALL they receive back when selling a card to the house.
Card Wall card pack pulls paid by players, minus refunded pulls and the $WALL paid back to winners who sell their card to the house.
Card Wall card pack pulls net of refunds and card buybacks, all kept by the Card Wall team; the cost of the prize cards is paid off chain and is not deducted.
Card Wall card pack pulls net of refunds and card buybacks, all withdrawn to the Card Wall team wallet; there are no $WALL buybacks or burns for holders.

USDC paid to launch a token, the 0.1% fee on public USDC committed during a guarded opening, and USDC-side Uniswap v3 LP fees generated by permanently locked Souless launch positions and collected on-chain.

The protocol-retained share of launch and collected LP fees, all guarded-opening fees, and any unallocated Launch Partner campaign remainder returned to the protocol by the LaunchPartnerPool. LP-fee revenue is the residual after creator, Community, actual active-partner, and active-referrer allocations.
The protocol-retained share of launch and collected LP fees, all guarded-opening fees, and unallocated Launch Partner campaign remainder, sent or claimable by the Souless treasury.

Launch fees allocated to narrative-protection holders and collected LP fees allocated on-chain to token creators, Community Mode stakers and InfoFi contributors, active Launch Partner slots, and active referrers. Community allocations use each credited epoch's stored staking share. Launch Partner revenue uses the partner amount actually allocated by LaunchPartnerPool rather than the gross campaign transfer.
Swap fees paid by users at each pool's fee tier, in the token each swap paid in.
Swap fees paid by users at each pool's fee tier, in the token each swap paid in, plus the arbitrage profit of the protocol's satellite pools.
The protocol fee (each pool's share of the swap fee, read from the pool: 1/4 on every pool since launch), the LP fees earned by protocol-owned liquidity, and all satellite arbitrage profit.

Half of the protocol fee, paid to the development fund, the LP fees earned by the protocol's own positions (its POL vaults and treasury Safe), and 87.5% of satellite arbitrage profit (12.5% to the development fund, 75% compounded into the treasury's satellite positions).
Swap fees less the protocol fee, earned by outside liquidity providers.
Half of the protocol fee and 12.5% of satellite arbitrage profit, sent to a fee jar that auctions it for GOO and burns the GOO.

Bonding-curve trading fees (1%, plus the snipe tax on buys in the first seconds after launch), creators' own taxes on curve trades, swap fees in graduated coins' Uniswap V3 pools, the ETH launch fee, the trade router's 0.05% fee on every trade sent from the site, and the protocol's share of every front-page bid: 25% of a bid on a coin launched here, all of a bid on a coin launched on PONS. A reward coin's transfer fee, a token tax paid in the launched coin, is not counted.

The protocol's share of trading fees and of the swap fees earned by locked graduation liquidity (each coin's immutable protocolShareBps, 30% at launch), launch fees, the trade router's fee, and the buyback and treasury shares of bids.
All revenue. It is split between the $OUTBID buyback vault and operations; $OUTBID has not launched, so none of it has reached token holders yet.
The creator's share of trading fees and of the locked position's swap fees, the creator's own tax, and the swap fees earned by third-party liquidity providers.
Total swap fees paid by traders on every swap.
Total swap fees paid by traders on Biatec's Algorand pools, from Biatec's own trade indexer (AVM Trade Reporter).
Portion of swap fees kept by the Biatec protocol.
Portion of swap fees distributed to liquidity providers.
Protocol fees from all visible Haedal lending vaults on that completed UTC day. Depositor yield is not included.
The same protocol fees, as reported in the endpoint's revenue field.
All reported revenue. It is paid to the vault fee recipient.
Assessment fees paid in USDC.
Assessment fees minus trader payouts and referral and affiliate commissions.
Trader payouts and referral and affiliate commissions paid out in USDC.
The router fee (1 basis point of the output amount) paid by users on every swap.
All router fees go to the vfat.io fee collector.

0.05% of the amount traded, collected by TRDEFI on positions created through its venue. The fee is embedded in the maker's signed order and paid to the receiver address when the position trades, so it is counted as the incoming token transfers it actually is. The fee rail has been in force since 2026-09-25; positions created before that carry no fee and are immutable.
The entire collected trading fee. TRDEFI retains 100% of it, with no share paid to suppliers or holders.
The entire collected trading fee, retained by TRDEFI.
Native-token fees paid by users for completed Primus verification reports.
The portion of verification fees paid to Primus.
The portion of verification fees paid to attestor node operators.

Launch fees, the 1% fee on curve trades, the 1% hook fee on swaps in graduated pools (all from the contracts' fee-accrual events), and the swap fee on frenlaunch's Doppler pools (ten times the platform's 10% integrator payout).

All launch fees, the platform's 25% of curve and graduated-pool trading fees, the platform's 10% integrator share of Doppler pool swap fees, and the 10% referrer seat on Doppler pools launched without a referrer (the platform holds that seat).

All launch fees and the platform's 25% of curve and graduated-pool trading fees, the platform's 10% integrator share of Doppler pool swap fees, and the 10% referrer seat on Doppler pools launched without a referrer (the platform holds that seat).

Curve and graduated pools: the creator's 75% of trading fees. Doppler pools: creator 60%, creator's referrer 10% (when the launch has one), re-invested liquidity 11.32%, Doppler 8.68% of the swap fee.

Everything users pay: the fee charged on each swap of a launched token, the higher fee charged in the first minutes after a launch, the fee to create a launch, and the fee the Peddles Terminal and trade bot add to a swap.
The protocol's share of each swap fee and of the opening fee, plus all launch fees and all Terminal and trade bot fees.
The share of each swap fee paid to the token's creator and to the token's own holders, and the part of the opening fee returned to the pool as liquidity.
Positive perpetual trading fees plus builder surcharges paid by users. Excludes funding payments and spot.
Fees minus supply-side revenue. Because rebates and the MegaPop contribution accrue on their own rules, this is negative when they exceed fees collected in the window.

Maker rebates, referral rebates, the full builder surcharge, and MegaPop prize-pool contributions. Each is a share of trading fees accrued on its own rule, and is not capped by the fees collected in the same window.
PopDEX does not buy back, burn, or distribute fees to token holders, so this is zero.

Traders pay a curve fee plus the launch's creator tax on every bonding-curve buy and sell, and an anti-snipe tax on buys made in the opening window. Swaps in a graduated Uniswap V4 pool pay the same creator tax plus a hook fee. Creators pay a flat launch fee in ETH when they launch a token.
All launch fees, bonding-curve trading fees and graduated-pool hook fees, counted when the curve or the hook distributes them.
The protocol's share of trading fees plus the launch fees in full.

The creator's share of bonding-curve and graduated-pool fees, plus the quote asset spent buying launch tokens back into the vesting vault. The buyback is funded out of the creator slice and buys the launch token, so it is a cost of funds rather than revenue the protocol keeps.
Trading fees on FAZE bonding curves and graduated pools, plus token launch and graduation fees. Settled fees are adjusted for opening and closing pending balances.

Fees retained by FAZE: platform treasury allocations plus creator fees from FAZE own-token pools. Excludes other projects creator allocations and fees allocated to locked liquidity. Buybacks are a subsequent capital allocation, not additional revenue.
Retained revenue after reclassifying net fees paid to the FAZE buyback burner; includes FAZE own-pool creator fees not yet distributed. This is revenue attribution, not a treasury cash balance.
Creator allocations for other launched tokens, including their own burners, plus fees allocated to locked liquidity. Pending allocations use the contracts live split at each boundary.

Native USDC fees paid by the hook to the designated FAZE buyback burner, less failed-payment recredits and actual keeper rewards. Recognized at funding rather than swap execution; excludes unrelated deposits and other tokens burners.

A 1% fee on every Loong trade, on the bonding curve and in graduated PancakeSwap Infinity pools (charged by the Loong hook), plus the launch-window anti-snipe tax (starts at 99% and decays to 0 over 3 seconds) and any token creation fee (currently 0).
The 0.10% platform share and the 0.10% $LOONG buyback-and-burn share of every trade, plus token creation fees.
The 0.10% platform share of every trade, plus token creation fees.
The 0.70% creator share of every trade, and the 0.10% used to buy back and burn the traded coin itself (except $LOONG).
The 0.10% of every trade that funds $LOONG buybacks and burns; on the $LOONG coin itself its own 0.10% coin buyback-and-burn share also buys $LOONG.
Builder-code fees paid by users trading Hyperliquid perps through the Kinetiq Markets interface.
Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid perps trades, retained entirely by Kinetiq.
Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid perps trades, all sent to Kinetiq.
The app's 0.1% interface fee on its Nordstern routes, paid by the trader.
The app's 0.1% interface fee on its Nordstern routes (Nordstern encodes it in 1/65536 steps, so 0.0992%), taken from each trade's output. Fees paid in GOO are valued at the trade's own price.
All interface fees go to the Goo Exchange treasury.
Swap fees estimated from each pool's configured fee tier and one token side of each swap. Excludes V2.5 pools.
Jumper platform fees (0-5 bps depending on the assets) paid by users on bridges.
Builder code fees on Hyperliquid and partner fees on Lighter, paid by users on perpetual trades placed through Jumper.
All builder code and partner fees on perpetual trades placed through Jumper, kept by Jumper.
All builder code and partner fees on perpetual trades placed through Jumper, sent to Jumper.
Traders pay the full 1.20% fee.
Every bonding curve trade pays 1.20%: a 0.70% protocol fee to Motoswap and a 0.50% fee to the coin creator.
The whole 0.70% protocol fee: the shares for MOTO stakers, MOTO buyback and burn, the treasury and the Rakeback program.
The treasury share and the Rakeback program share of the 0.70% protocol fee.
The 0.50% creator fee to coin creators.
The share of the 0.70% protocol fee paid to MOTO stakers plus the share used to buy back and burn MOTO.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perpetual trades placed through DXAP (0.1% until 2026-07-09, 0.01% until 2026-09-03, 0.025% since); excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
Builder code fees collected by DXAP from Hyperliquid perpetual trades.
1% of every trade on the bonding curve and in the graduated Uniswap v4 pools, plus the flat USDC fee paid to launch a coin.
30% of every trading fee and every launch fee, sent to the Lockcurve treasury.
70% of every trading fee, paid to the coin's creator.
ORBIO creator and LP fees collected in harvests plus CREDIT order-book buyer fees swept by staking, excluding CREDIT activation burns and launchpad ORBIO fees.
Harvest and order-book fees allocated to treasury and ORBIO token holders.
The treasury share of harvests plus swept order-book fees, including the harvest backing share when no ORBIO is staked.
The harvest share allocated as inference backing to ORBIO stakers, valued in USDG when funded rather than when claimed.

Two things, and they are different money, and only the first of them is paid by anyone: it is reported as the user fee as well. First, the fee a trader paid on a swap in a pool the plugin runs in, at the rate the plugin set for that swap; the plugin takes no share of that fee, so nothing of it is charged to the user on the protocol's behalf. Second, the arbitrage the plugin realised inside the pool and paid out, read from the ProfitDistributed event where a deployment settles through a distributor and from the donatedToLps leg of ProfitShared where the plugin pays the pool's liquidity providers directly.

The protocol's share of the captured arbitrage, taken from the distributor's own share config as it stood at the block of each capture. Nothing of the swap fee is the protocol's, and the captures donated straight to liquidity providers leave it nothing either.
The swap fee in full, which the pool's liquidity providers and its AMM earn, plus the part of every capture that the share config pays to the pool's beneficiaries.

All yield generated by Arrowfarm concentrated liquidity vaults: LP trading fees and gauge rewards harvested by the strategies, the performance fee charged on them, and trading fees sent straight to the treasury.
Performance fees charged on harvests (arrow fee and strategist fee, paid in WETH) plus trading fees that strategies send to the treasury. The harvest caller fee is not counted as revenue.
Strategist performance fees and trading fees sent to the Arrowfarm treasury.
Yield that stays with vault depositors after the performance fee (LP trading fees and gauge rewards), plus the harvest caller fee paid to whoever calls harvest.
The arrow performance fee in WETH is sent to the ArrowBuybackBurner, which buys ARROWFARM and burns it.

Platform fees paid by GDEX users. Solana: received in SOL by the GDEX treasury, 1% of the SOL side of each swap and 0.1% on SOL withdrawals (1% when bridging). EVM chains: the 1% swap fee paid to the GDEX treasury by the KyberSwap router GDEX routes swaps through; EVM transfer and bridge fees are not included.
Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on perpetual trades placed through GDEX.
Hyperliquid builder code fees collected by GDEX. Referral rewards GDEX later pays out off-chain from its treasury are not deducted.
Builder code fees paid on trades routed through Hypercall; excludes Hyperliquid trading fees.
Builder code fees collected by Hypercall on those trades.
Builder code fees retained by Hypercall on those trades.
Traders pay all of the fees above.
Every trade pays the pair swap fee (0.30%) to liquidity providers, a 0.70% Motoswap protocol fee on the quote side, and on coins that graduated from moto.fun a 0.30% creator fee.
The 0.30% pair fee to liquidity providers and the creator fee to coin creators.
Same as Fees - traders pay all of it; liquidity providers are not charged.

Everything traders pay on a swap: the pool's swap fee from the Swap event (protocol fee included), plus what a Latch launch pool's guard takes itself - the creator tax, and on newer launch guards the guard's part of the trade fee - read from the guard's TaxTaken and FeeTaken events. Only Latch's own launch guards are read.

What reaches the protocol, counted when the fee is taken: the protocol fee each Swap event carries; the protocol's share of a launch pool's liquidity fees under the pool's permanent LP lock split, only where the locks provably hold all of the pool's liquidity; and the protocol's share of the creator tax and guard trade fee under the split the guard stores for that pool. A split that cannot be read is never guessed: that amount is left out of Revenue.
All of Revenue. Latch has no token, so nothing is diverted to holders.

Fees minus Revenue: swap fees earned by liquidity providers, and the shares of locked-liquidity fees, creator tax and guard trade fees that go to launch creators and integrators (and any guard-taken amount whose split could not be read).
Aerodrome LP fees distributed to MAMO stakers.
Aerodrome LP trading fees distributed to MAMO stakers via the multi-rewards contract.
Users pay the full TRNCH integrator fee.

Integrator fee TRNCH adds to swaps and bridges made on TRNCH (0.5% on a single swap, 1% on a swap of a token from the TRNCH Heat ranking or on a basket of swaps, 1% on bridges, 0.5% on swaps built through the TRNCH Bot API and MCP server for AI agents), paid to the TRNCH treasury Safe through LI.FI, KyberSwap, 0x, Uniswap, SushiSwap and 1inch. Router and DEX fees are excluded.
All integrator fees received by the TRNCH treasury Safe are kept by TRNCH.
All integrator fees go to the TRNCH treasury.

All swap fees paid by traders on ADEXTO bonding curves, read from each Swap event: the creator, curve reserve, buyback and protocol legs. Rates are set per market at launch and never change; the launch presets are 1.00% on factory 1.0.0 and 0.12.0 markets and 0.40% on factory 0.11.0 markets.

The protocol leg of every swap, paid to the ADEXTO protocol treasury: 0.10% of the trade on factory 0.11.0, 0.12.0 and 1.0.0 markets, where it is a factory constant. Factory 0.10.0 markets have no protocol leg.
The creator leg paid to each market's creator, the reserve leg that stays in the market's curve, and the buyback leg that buys and burns the market's own token.
Borrow origination, repayment and explicit liquidation fees, and lending entry and exit fees, valued in USD when charged.
All of the fees (Borrow, Repay, Deposit, Withdraw); the protocol keeps them in full.

All of the fees (Borrow, Repay, Deposit, Withdraw): 77% is set aside for $LOAN buybacks at token launch and 23% goes to the treasury. No buyback has executed yet; holders revenue will be reported once they do.

Carriers pay XNET for mobile data offloaded onto WiFi. Until settlement arrives, Fees are conservatively accrued from measured daily offload. Closed unsettled months use XNET's official monthly projection and newer days use a conservative API-GB rate. Carrier payments typically settle about two months later, and historical accrual is reconciled to the amount actually paid.

Historically 20% of ordinary carrier Fees was allocated to operations. Under passed XIP-12, Protocol Revenue is 40%: 20% operations and 20% protocol-owned liquidity. For the XIP-13.1 fiat slice, 20% is retained for XNET operations.

Passed XIP-13.1 lets designated operators choose fiat instead of token distributions. Their 75% operator cash share is Supply-Side Revenue and is attributed to the service month reconciled by the carrier settlement that funds the payout, preserving the observed NET60+ settlement cadence.

Accrued service-period tokenholder allocation. Historically 80% of ordinary carrier Fees accrued to buyback-and-burn; under passed XIP-12, 60% does. The XIP-13.1 fiat slice contributes its 5% facilitation/BBB allocation. Values are provisional wherever the underlying Fees are provisional and reconcile with settlement. This is accrual attribution; actual on-chain buyback or burn execution can occur later.
Builder fees received by crotrade from trades on Polymarket v2
No builder fees are kept by crotrade
Builder fees received by crotrade, all distributed to its token holders
Every trading fee cro.trade users pay on spot trades routed through cro.trade's contracts on Cronos and Robinhood Chain.

Every trading fee cro.trade users pay on spot trades routed through cro.trade's contracts on Cronos and Robinhood Chain, measured from the fee each trade pays on-chain. Trades whose fee leaves no on-chain event are not included, so the figure is a floor.
All trading fees; no share goes to liquidity providers.
None, all trading fees go to CRONUS holders.
All trading fees go to CRONUS holders through buybacks: distributed to holders before 2026-09-22, burned since.

Actual quote-asset swap charges emitted by the verified TaxHook FeesAccrued event. V1 launches charge no trading tax. No token mint allocation, gas, deposits, claim payments or buyback execution is counted as a new fee.
Treasury allocation of each fee on an accrual basis; excludes creators, referrers and launched-token buybacks.
The same treasury allocation as Revenue. Fledgo has no own-token holder revenue.

Creator recipients, attributed referrers and launched-token buyback allocations. Missing referrers retain their allocation for creators. Buybacks benefit the launched token, not a Fledgo governance token.
Bridge fees paid by users on completed transfers.
Bridge fees retained by LilSwap after partner share.
Bridge fees paid to bridge providers and partners.

Yield from RealFi's reserve portfolio (treasury bills, money market funds, CLO ETFs, floating-rate bonds and private credit), counted when it is minted on-chain as new USDrf at each weekly staking epoch, net of portfolio losses burned from the sUSDrf staking vault. Excludes income RealFi earns off-chain on unstaked USDrf reserves that is never minted on-chain. Mint and redeem fees are currently 0 bps.
Share of each epoch's minted yield sent to the RealFi protocol fee address instead of the sUSDrf staking vault.
Share of each epoch's minted yield added to the sUSDrf staking vault, which raises the USDrf redeemable per sUSDrf, net of portfolio losses burned from the vault.

ZC burned by users to publish in the Book, relay fees on private posts, payments and withdrawals, and deposit vetting fees of the ZC privacy pool. The launcher share of Stockereum's swap fee on ZC trades is a token tax and is not counted.
All fees: burns accrue to holders, the rest to the protocol; no supply-side payments except relay fees earned by third-party relayers.
Relay fees earned by the team-run relayer and deposit vetting fees kept by the Entrypoint.
Relay fees on zipcoin Entrypoint withdrawals submitted by relayers other than the team's.
ZC permanently burned by users to post.
All escrow fees are paid directly by the trading users.

Escrow fees paid by sellers and buyers on completed P2P trades, read from EscrowComplete events. Fees are tiered by trade size (fixed fee below 50 USD, then 1.25% down to 0.25%) with a lower rate for verified merchants. Cancelled or refunded trades pay no fee.
All escrow fees are kept by the protocol.
All escrow fees go to the protocol treasury.
Same as Fees: all of it is paid by quest creators, advertisers and badge minters. Joining a quest and claiming a reward are free.

Everything PeddleQuest charges: the fee quest creators pay on top of the reward pool they deposit, the flat quest creation fee, the protocol's share of rewards that winners did not claim before the deadline, payments for trending and banner promotion slots, and the fee users pay to mint an optional completion badge.
All fees (quest creation, deposit, unclaimed, promotion and badge) are kept by the protocol. Quest rewards themselves go to winners and are not counted as fees or revenue.
Fees (quest creation, deposit, unclaimed, promotion and badge) accrued to the protocol treasury (a Safe multisig).
The share of badge mint fees routed on-chain to buyback and burn. Zero while that route is switched off, which it has been since launch.

0.5% protocol fee on shielded pool deposits and 0.5% on withdrawals (Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, Avalanche, Solana), deposit check fees on Solana, plus ZEC rewards received by the Nullmask team wallet from MASK token holder distributions (Solana).
Lock creation fees paid by users to Titan Locker, read from FeeCollected events on every lock manager: a flat ETH fee, or a share of the deposited token for ERC-20 and vesting locks.
All lock creation fees go to the Titan Locker fee receiver.
No fees are shared with liquidity providers or other parties.
Titan Locker has no token, so no fees go to token holders.
Copy trading fees paid by fomo-mcp users. Excludes the $FOMOMCP creator fees, which are paid by $FOMOMCP traders.
Copy trading fees fomo-mcp users pay on every copied buy and sell (1% on copies under $100, 0.5% from $100), plus the creator fees of the fomo-mcp token $FOMOMCP on the Pons launchpad.
All fees (copy trading fees and $FOMOMCP creator fees) are kept by fomo-mcp.
Bonding-curve fee paid in the native token on every launchpad buy and sell.
Launchpad fee kept by Crystal after the token creator's split.
Launchpad fee paid to the token creator.
USDW trading fees accrued to the protocol, measured as the increase in FeeRouter.totalPlatformFees() on each chain where Wager Predict is deployed.
The same increase in FeeRouter.totalPlatformFees(). That counter is the platform's collected trading fees.
The increase in FeeRouter.totalPlatformFees() kept by the protocol.
Fees charged on bets, paid by players.
Fees charged on bets in every V5, V6 and V7 room: the room stakers' fee (V5 / V6), the platform fee and the room creator's fee.
The platform fee on bets, sent to the ElcasTreasury (V5) or the ElcasBurner (V6, V7).
The fee kept by each room's pool for its stakers and the fee paid to each room's creator.
The ElcasTreasury / ElcasBurner swaps the platform fee to $ELCAS and burns it.
Open and close fees and borrow paid by traders.
Open and close fees (a share of the position size, set per market) and hourly borrow paid by traders.
The platform's share of open and close fees (currently 10 %), accrued for the platform's fee address.
The platform's share of open and close fees, accrued for the platform's fee address.
The rest of the open and close fees and all borrow go to each market's LP vault; the market's creator takes up to 20 % of the open and close fees.
The fee taken from each settled round's losing side.
The fee taken from each settled round's losing side (set per market, up to 6 %).
The platform's share of each round's fee (currently 1 % of the losing side).
The platform's share of each round's fee, accrued for the platform's fee address.
The market's house vault LPs, the market's creator and whoever settles the round (bounty).
Total fees paid by users for bridge and swap txs.
Protocol revenue is currently 0.
Pheasant Network currently takes no protocol fee.
All fees paid by users go to the relayers.
Revenue distributed to token holders is currently 0.
Platform fees, integrator app fees and swap costs paid by users on Relay bridges and swaps, excluding execution costs (network gas).
Platform fees. This is an upper bound: Relay pays qualifying integrators an undisclosed 0-67% revenue share out of it.
Platform fees kept by Relay. This is an upper bound: Relay pays qualifying integrators an undisclosed 0-67% revenue share out of it.
App fees paid to the integrators that add them, and swap costs paid to liquidity providers. Excludes the integrator revenue share of the platform fee, which Relay does not disclose.
Fees paid on room-key buys and sells, the flat fee to launch a room token, and swap fees earned by room-token liquidity. Excludes fees on Spot swaps routed through third-party aggregators.
AlfaClub's platform key-trading fee, room-token launch fees and 15% of room-token swap fees, plus the creator shares in AlfaClub's own room, the room behind the ALFA token.
Creator key-trading fees, plus 85% of room-token swap fees: 50% to the room's keyholders and 35% to the creator. Creator shares in AlfaClub's own room count as Revenue instead.

Pons creator fees paid to Mosh bundles (each bundle's swarm contract), plus the one-time raise fee Mosh takes when a bundle launches. The creator fees are also counted by Pons V2 as its creators' share, so this adapter is marked as double counted.

Mosh's share of the creator fees (creatorFeeShareBps, 20% at launch), the raise fee (raiseFeeBps, 5% of the filled raise), and, where the Mosh treasury holds a bundle's fee claims itself, its pro-rata part of the backers' share.
The bundle backers' share of the creator fees (80% at launch), including any team share a bundle's creator set out of it, less the part the Mosh treasury holds as a backer.
Trading fees and builder fees paid on Derive perpetual trades.
Trading fees minus maker rebates.
Maker rebates and builder fees.
Trading fees and builder fees paid on Derive options trades.
Trading fees minus maker rebates, minus the fees spent on DRV buybacks (negative on buyback days).
DRV bought back with a share of fees from all Derive markets (options, perps and spot), held by the Derive DAO treasury.
Trading fees and builder fees paid on Derive spot trades.
SunSwap V4 charges no protocol fee, so the protocol keeps no revenue.
Builder-code fees paid by users trading Hyperliquid spot through the Kinetiq Markets interface.
Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid spot trades, retained entirely by Kinetiq.
Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid spot trades, all sent to Kinetiq.
Fees users pay when closing or settling HIP-4 outcome positions, including builder-code fees added by front-ends. Hyperliquid charged no outcome fee of its own before 15 Aug 2026.
99% of outcome fees net of builder-code fees, sent to the Assistance Fund to buy HYPE.
Hyperliquid's protocol keeps no outcome fees; they go to the Assistance Fund and the HLP vault.
Builder-code fees paid to the front-ends that routed the trades, plus 1% of the remaining outcome fees to HLP vault depositors.
99% of outcome fees net of builder-code fees, used by the Assistance Fund to buy back HYPE.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perps trades placed through CoinDCX.
Builder code fees collected by CoinDCX from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perps trades placed through Bitget Wallet.
Builder code fees collected by Bitget Wallet from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perps trades placed through HyperLink.
Builder code fees collected by HyperLink from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perps trades placed through Borsa.
Builder code fees collected by Borsa from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perps trades placed through TrueNorth.
Builder code fees collected by TrueNorth from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perps trades placed through Velo.
Builder code fees collected by Velo from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perps trades placed through TopNod.
Builder code fees collected by TopNod from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perps trades placed through Aura.
Builder code fees collected by Aura from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perps trades placed through Dapital.
Builder code fees collected by Dapital from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perps trades placed through Pluto.
Builder code fees collected by Pluto from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perps trades placed through Sendai.
Builder code fees collected by Sendai from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Builder-code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid spot trades placed through the builder code.
Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid spot trades, all kept by the builder.
Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid spot trades, all sent to the builder's protocol.
2% fee on realized PnL at close, 2% fee on margin lost in liquidations, and LP profits above the $5M cap swept to PAPER stakers. Trader wins and losses that stay in the LP are not counted.
All fees: half of the 2% fees to PAPER stakers, half to the dev fee recipient, and LP profits above the $5M cap to PAPER stakers.
Half of the 2% close and liquidation fees, paid to the dev fee recipient.
Half of the 2% close and liquidation fees plus LP profits above the $5M cap, paid in USDC to PAPER stakers.
Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on trades placed through Auspex; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
Builder code fees collected by Auspex. Referral rewards Auspex later pays out from its treasury are not deducted.
The protocol's share of open and close fees (currently 10 %), collected in the protocol's FeeVault.
The protocol's share of open and close fees, collected in the protocol's FeeVault.
All swap fees are paid by the swapper.

Swap fee charged on the output token of each swap (protocol share plus LP share), read from the Swapped event. The coverage toll a swap may pay when it drains a leg below its coverage floor stays in the leg's reserves as a buffer and is not counted.
Protocol share (protoFee) of the swap fee. Zero on coop fills, which book no protocol fee.
The protocol share (protoFee) of the swap fee goes to the BTR treasury.
LP share (lpFee) of the swap fee, accrued to the liquidity providers of the output leg.
SOL service fees paid by users to Tsunammi for the Create Token flow.
All tracked Create Token service fees are retained as Tsunammi protocol revenue.
SOL received by Tsunammi's dedicated Create Token fee collector.
What traders pay: the bonding curve fee, the referral fee Ryntra earns on graduated-pool trades and the graduated pool's fees; not the migration fee, which comes out of the curve's reserve.

Everything traders pay on the bonding curves of tokens launched with Ryntra Launch (Meteora DBC pools on its configs, created by its pool payer), including the 20% Meteora keeps; after graduation, the referral fee Meteora pays Ryntra on trades made through Ryntra; and what Ryntra takes as the partner of a graduated curve (its share of the migration fee, and later the fees of the DAMM v2 liquidity locked for it) when its fee claimer withdraws them. The creator's share of the migration fee and the quote above the graduation threshold (not a fee) are not included.
Ryntra's 60% of the configs' share of the bonding curve fee, the referral fees Meteora pays it, and its graduation income when withdrawn.

Ryntra's 60% of the configs' share of the bonding curve fee, the referral fees Meteora pays it and its graduation income, all of it for the protocol: Ryntra has no token and distributes nothing to holders.
The token creator's 40% of the configs' share of the bonding curve fee, Meteora's protocol fee, and the referral fees Meteora pays other apps.
Fees traders pay Ryntra inside the trades they make through it.

Fees people pay Ryntra on trades made through it. On Solana: what the swap router (Jupiter, or DFlow when Jupiter routes through it) pays into Ryntra's fee wallet and its Jupiter referral account inside the trade. On Arc: the developer fee of a Circle swap and the fee leg of a KyberSwap swap that name Ryntra's fee address, read from Circle's fee collector and KyberSwap's router events. Plain transfers into these accounts are not fees.

Trading fees kept by Ryntra: the whole fee paid into its fee wallet on Solana and from KyberSwap on Arc, what reached its Jupiter referral account less Jupiter's 20% share, and the Circle developer fee less the share (about 10%) Circle's fee collector routes to its protocol recipient. Cashback and invite rewards are paid later, when people claim them, and are not deducted.
Trading fees kept by Ryntra, all of it for the protocol: Ryntra has no token and distributes nothing to holders.

Jupiter's 20% share of the fees that reached Ryntra's Jupiter referral account, and the share (about 10%) of the Circle developer fee that Circle's fee collector routes to its protocol recipient on Arc.

Commission SX Bet takes on the profit of winning bets, counted when the escrow pays it to SX's fee wallet at settlement. On V3 the rates are set per account and can apply to singles as well as parlays; losing and voided bets pay nothing.
Commission taken from the profit of winning bets and kept by SX. Market makers get none of it.
All commission goes to SX: first a fee wallet, and from 4 September 2026 the treasury contract that also holds the SX community fund.
Zero. Market makers get no share of the commission.

Everything charged on the launchpad: DEEP's fee on each bonding-curve buy and sell (1.25%), the reward fee a token's creator chose at launch (0% to 5% of each trade), the fee to launch a token ($2, paid in SOL) and the migration fee taken from the SOL a curve raised when its token graduates (1%, less the network rent of the new pool's accounts).
DEEP's share: its 1.25% fee on bonding-curve trades, the token launch fees and the migration fees. Reward fees are not included.

DEEP's 1.25% fee on bonding-curve trades, the token launch fees and the migration fees, all paid into DEEP's on-chain fee vault, which pays 10% to the team that builds DEEP and 90% to the DEEP treasury.
The reward fee of each token, paid in full to the token's creator or, for a Holder Rewards token, to the holders of that token.

Everything charged on DeepSwap: the swap fee (0.35% of a buy and 0.75% of a sell), the reward fee the pool charges on top of it (0% to 5%, fixed when the pool was created) and the flat fee in SOL to open a pool. Pools of graduated launchpad tokens are opened by the launchpad, which pays that fee out of the token's migration fee; it is reported with the launchpad, not here.
DEEP's share of the swap fee (0.25% of a buy, 0.65% of a sell) and the pool creation fees.
