DEEP's share of the swap fee (0.25% of a buy, 0.65% of a sell) and the pool creation fees, all paid into DEEP's on-chain fee vault, which pays 10% to the team that builds DEEP and 90% to the DEEP treasury.

The liquidity providers' share of the swap fee (0.10% of each swap, left in the pool) and each pool's reward fee, paid in full to the pool's creator or, on a Holder Rewards pool, to the holders of the pool's token.
QUOTUM trading tax collected by TaxSink, measured in NVDA when claimed, excluding Pons platform fees and direct funding transfers.
Claimed QUOTUM trading tax less the NVDA forwarded to pay inference providers; NVDA forwarded to fund the protocol's own trading agent stays in revenue.
The fixed 40% share of claimed QUOTUM trading tax transferred to the protocol recipient in NVDA.
NVDA forwarded from TaxSink to pay inference providers, excluding the portion the team reports moving on to fund the protocol's trading agent.

Successful buyback NVDA is booked only in hours with burns, capped at positive revenue from UTC midnight through that hour, after subtracting earlier holders bookings that day. No holders revenue is booked when that budget is zero or negative. Excess reserve-funded spending, failed purchases and direct token burns are excluded.

Trading fees paid by users on every Vaultex coin: 2% of each buy and sell on the bonding curve, in the coin's quote asset (SOL, USDC and more), read from Meteora DBC swap events. Most of it goes to the coin creator, split by the creator percentage of each Vaultex pool config (DBC create-config event).
Vaultex's share of the trading fee on every bonding-curve trade, claimed into the Vaultex treasury.
The coin creator's share of every trade (which creators can share with their holders through Drip and Drop), Meteora's protocol fee, and the referral fee paid to the frontend that hosted the swap.
The 0.5% fee users pay on every swap made through Monolith Exchange.
The 0.5% fee users pay on every swap made through Monolith Exchange, collected by Jupiter into Monolith's referral fee accounts.
The 80% of the 0.5% swap fee that Monolith Exchange keeps after Jupiter's 20% share.
The 80% of the 0.5% swap fee that goes to the Monolith Exchange treasury.
The 20% of the 0.5% swap fee that Jupiter keeps as the routing provider.
The 4% paid by the owner who repays the loan.
On repayment, 3% of principal is paid to the funder and 1% of principal is paid to the protocol. The principal returned to the funder is not a fee.
The 1% protocol fee paid to the protocol address on repayment.
The 3% paid to the funder when the owner repays.
BOT paid by consumers to request AI inference.

BOT paid by consumers to request AI inference, plus forfeited dispute bonds. Inference fees are counted when a request is fulfilled - timed-out requests refund in full, so escrowed-only requests are excluded.
The protocol's share (protocolFeeBps, currently 10%) of each fulfilled inference fee, plus forfeited challenge bonds, accrued to the treasury.
The treasury share of each fulfilled inference fee plus forfeited dispute bonds.
The operator's share of each fulfilled inference fee, paid on fulfillment.

Swap fees charged by DeepCore pools, read from each Swap event (protocol fee included), plus the fee DeepCore's router charges on fills it routes to other venues, read from its Filled events. Launch-pool creator taxes and launch-guard trade fees are not counted.
The protocol fee slice each Swap event carried, plus the router fee on routed fills. Both are paid to the protocol.
The rest of each swap fee, earned by liquidity providers.

Pack purchases minus USDC returned to players: refunds of cancelled pulls, card cash-outs, sell-backs, USDC prizes and reimbursed card shipments. This is the 10% fee Raflux keeps when a card is exchanged for USDC plus the game result of pulls, so it is negative on days when players win more than they pay.
Pack purchases minus USDC returned to players, kept by Raflux. No share goes to LPs, referrers or token holders.
Pack purchases minus USDC returned to players, all of it sent to the Raflux treasury.
Protocol share of swap fees, read per pool from the vault (protocol swap fee set by the protocol fee controller).
Protocol share of swap fees, which goes to the Bush treasury.
Swap fees kept by liquidity providers, plus the pool creator fee where a pool sets one.
Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on perpetual trades placed through Kokoah; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
Builder code fees collected by Kokoah. Referral rewards Kokoah later pays out off-chain from these fees are not deducted.

The desk's fee on the gross premium of each weekly call the vault sells (20% at launch), fixed at the sale and recognized one hour later when the Safe can no longer void the sale; a voided sale charges no fee. The premium itself is not counted as fees: it is the buyer's payment for the option, which depositors carry against the risk of the call settling in the money (see the options adapter's premium volume). A call sold outside the desk (not possible with the current operator) counts the fee the operator reports at settlement.
All of the desk fee on the gross premium of each weekly call the vault sells, paid to the HedgeHood treasury Safe at settlement.
On-chain BUY fee from FillEvent, paid by traders (SELLs and settlements are fee-free).
On-chain BUY fee from FillEvent (SELLs and settlements are fee-free).
100% protocol revenue — no LPs, no token, no revenue share.
Trading fees paid on sprout.fun bonding curves (1% or 3% per launch) and in the Choice v2 pools that launches graduate into (same rate, taken by the Sprout hook).
Trading fees minus the share credited to launch creators and referrers (the platform share).
Part of the platform share that is not used for SPROUT buyback and burn.
Share of trading fees credited to launch creators, and on the curve to referrers.
80% of the platform share funds SPROUT buyback and burn (ratio taken from the Sprout docs).
Users pay a 0.25% fee on each swap.
Each swap pays a 0.25% fee.
1/6 of swap fees (~0.0417%) accrue to the protocol via the factory feeTo LP mint.
1/6 of swap fees (~0.0417%) go to the protocol feeTo address.
5/6 of swap fees (~0.2083%) go to liquidity providers.

The service fees copypump charges on every copied buy and sell, collected as a USDC transfer to the copypump treasury and counted on the day it is collected (the collector batches fees per user, so a fee can land the day after its trade).

The service fee copypump charges on every copied buy and sell, collected as a USDC transfer to the copypump treasury and counted on the day it is collected (the collector batches fees per user, so a fee can land the day after its trade).
Fees minus the fee payer cost: what copypump keeps. The 'app revenue, after gas' figure on copypumpfun.com/data.
Fees minus the fee payer cost: what copypump keeps.

The cost copypump pays on users' behalf: the SOL the copypump fee payer loses co-signing every copied trade (signature fee, priority fee, rent of the token accounts the route creates), net of the rent it recovers when the emptied accounts are closed back to it. Priced at the daily SOL price.

1% swap fees on Pumper-launched tokens' Uniswap V3 pools and on the PUMPER pools, plus creator-set buy/sell taxes and the V4 hook / Lock-curve fees (1% base fee + tax) on Pumper-launched tokens. Launched tokens are taken from PumperProtocolRegistry.
15% of every launched token's fees and taxes: 10% to adminVault and 5% to the PUMPER buy-and-burn vault. PUMPER's own pool fees carry no protocol cut.
The 10% of launched token fees and taxes paid to adminVault, the protocol treasury.

5% of launched token fees and taxes sent to the FEFER buy-and-burn vault (FEFER is a separate token), and 80% split between each token's creator, stakers, buyback-and-burn and liquidity in a ratio the creator fixes at launch; plus 100% of PUMPER pool fees, paid to its LPs.
The 5% of launched token fees and taxes sent to the PUMPER buy-and-burn vault, which buys and burns PUMPER.
Service fees and Polymarket builder fees, both paid by the trader on every Polymarket buy and sell routed through Polycool.

Service fees charged by Polycool on every Polymarket buy and sell routed through the app (1.00% of the notional for new users, decreasing with lifetime volume to 0.50% above $100K, pulled from the trader's wallet into the Polycool treasury as USDC.e or pUSD), plus the Polymarket builder fees on those trades, which the trader pays inside Polymarket's trade fee and Polymarket pays out to Polycool daily.
Service fees and Polymarket builder fees, minus referral rewards paid out. No liquidity providers.
Service fees and Polymarket builder fees kept by Polycool after referral rewards are paid out.

Referral rewards: referrers earn 25% of the service fees generated by the users they referred. Counted when paid, as pUSD transfers from the referral payout wallet (the treasury since 2026-10-22) to referrers (claims before 2026-07-01, about $270 in total, were paid from the treasury and are not tracked).
The 1% fee paid by traders on every Ferzan coin before it graduates.
The 1% bonding curve trading fee on every Ferzan coin before it graduates (Meteora's DBC fee on Solana, including Meteora's protocol share).
Ferzan's share of the curve fee: 50%, less 10% to a referrer when one is set. On Solana, half of the DBC trading fee.
The coin creator's 50%, referrer payouts, and on Solana Meteora's protocol fee.
None.

The launchpad's 0.25% platform fee and the creator's 0.5% fee on every Incognito Launchpad bonding-curve trade, plus the quote-side trading fees of graduated launches' locked liquidity, all paid by traders.

Fees paid by traders of coins launched on Incognito Launchpad (Solana): the launchpad's 0.25% platform fee and the coin creator's 0.5% fee on every trade against the Raydium LaunchLab bonding curves it configures, and, once a coin graduates, the quote-side trading fees of its permanently locked liquidity, harvested with the Fee Key the launchpad holds. Raydium's own protocol fee is excluded. Amounts are in each pool's quote token.
The platform fee and the harvested locked-liquidity fees, both received by the launchpad treasury.
The 0.25% platform fee on bonding-curve trades and the harvested locked-liquidity fees, all sent to the launchpad treasury.
The creator fee of each bonding-curve trade, paid to the wallet that launched the coin.
Actual Hyperliquid builder fees paid on Ditto-routed perpetual trades; excludes venue trading fees.
Builder fees collected by Ditto on its routed perpetual trades.
SOL paid by Peep users: the 0.75% fee on swaps between SOL and a token.

SOL paid to Peep by its users: the 0.75% fee on swaps between SOL and a token made in Peep. Swaps between SOL and USDC/USDT, token-to-token swaps and tips carry no Peep fee. Peep's 5% share of paid group joins is not counted: a group join carries no on-chain marker that tells it apart from any transaction with the same two transfers.
SOL kept by Peep: the whole 0.75% fee on swaps between SOL and a token.
SOL received by the Peep treasury: the whole 0.75% fee on swaps between SOL and a token.
None: Peep shares no part of its swap fee with referrers, integrators or Jupiter.
Every fee traders pay on Bordrless DEX trades: the protocol fee, LP fee, coin creator fee and holder reward fee.
Every fee traders pay on trades on the Bordrless DEX, including launched coins after they graduate: the protocol fee, LP fee, coin creator fee and holder reward fee.
The protocol fee, paid to the Bordrless treasury: half is kept, half buys back $BORDR.
Half of the protocol fee, kept by the treasury.
Fees paid to liquidity providers, coin creators and coin holders.
Half of the protocol fee, spent buying back $BORDR.
Every fee traders pay on Bordrless launchpad bonding curve trades: the protocol fee, LP fee, coin creator fee and holder reward fee.
Every fee traders pay on trades on the Bordrless launchpad bonding curve, before a coin graduates: the protocol fee, LP fee, coin creator fee and holder reward fee.
Creator trading fees paid by traders of Credence tokens on Pons, and the Credence fee paid by token creators at launch.
Creator trading fees that Pons pays to Credence vaults for the tokens Credence deployed, creator fees paid into creator vaults for X accounts, and the Credence fee charged on every launch.
What Credence keeps: 20% of each token vault's creator fees, which buys back and burns $PFWA, the protocol's cut of creator vault fees, and launch fees.
Revenue sent to the Credence Safe: the protocol's cut of creator vault fees and the launch fees.

80% of each token vault's creator fees, bridged to Polygon to fund the token's Polymarket bet (whose winnings buy back and burn the token), and the creator vault fees held for the X account they belong to.
The 20% of each token vault's creator fees that is spent buying $PFWA sent to the dead address, counted when the fees are collected.
Everything traders and market creators pay on PFWA Markets: trading fees, early-sell penalties and market creation fees.

Everything traders and market creators pay on PFWA Markets: the trading fee on buys and on sells after a market's deadline, the early-sell penalty on sells before the deadline, and the fee to create a market. Activity of PFWA's own wallets (team, market seeder, market-making agent) is excluded.

The protocol's share of all fees: the protocol's leg of every trading fee (both legs on markets the protocol created), half of every early-sell penalty, and the market creation fee, including the part spent buying back and burning $PFWA.

The fees sent to the PFWA treasury: the protocol's leg of every trading fee (both legs on markets the protocol created), half of every early-sell penalty, and the part of each market creation fee not used for the $PFWA buyback.
The market creator's leg of the trading fee on markets created by users, and the half of each early-sell penalty paid into the market's bonus pot for the winning side.
ETH spent buying $PFWA that is burned: half of each v2 market creation fee is swapped for $PFWA in the same transaction and sent to the dead address.
The 5% of the ETH side of every swap in a Sherwood game pool, paid by the swapper into the round's prize pot.
The 5% of the ETH side of every swap in a Sherwood game pool that is paid into the round's prize pot. Direct deposits into the pots are not fees and are excluded.
The share of the pot fees that buys back and burns $PFWA: 10% in Season 1 (ETH/$PFWA pool) and 7% in Season 2 (ETH/$IMD pool) of what is left after the Dice randomness fees.
Zero: the protocol keeps none of the pot fees.

The Dice Protocol fees paid from the pot for Flip moves, then the share of the remaining pot fees paid to players: the round's prizes (80% in Season 1, 78% in Season 2), the share rolled into the next round's pot (10% and 5%), and in Season 2 the 10% that buys back and burns $IMD, the game pool's token.

The share of the pot fees spent buying back and burning $PFWA (10% in Season 1, 7% in Season 2, after Dice randomness fees), counted when the swap pays the fee. Burns funded by direct pot deposits are excluded.

Fees paid by traders on MoveFast launchpad pools: the platform trading fee, any pool fee, and the token tax each launch's creator sets. The part of the tax that burns the launched token is not included.
The platform trading fee on every MoveFast trade (1.5% of the trade), sent to the MoveFast treasury.
The token tax paid out to holders and creators of the launched tokens, plus any pool fee kept in the pool's reserves.
Instant redeem/unstake fees paid by users to skip the delayed exit flow, valued in UBTC.

Settled yield from mxBTC's HyperCore funding strategy after borrowing and trading costs, converted to UBTC and measured at distribution, plus instant redeem/unstake fees; excludes unsettled strategy income.
The foundation's share of settled mxBTC yield plus instant redeem/unstake fees, valued in UBTC.
The foundation's share of settled mxBTC yield plus instant redeem/unstake fees retained by the protocol, valued in UBTC.
Settled yield allocated to smxBTC stakers and the insurance-fund reserve that backstops mxBTC.
Swap fees paid by traders on Choice v1 pools, which is 0.3% of the swap output.
One sixth of each swap fee, kept by the protocol in the Choice treasury multisig.
One sixth of each swap fee, sent to the Choice treasury multisig.
Five sixths of each swap fee: two thirds stays in the pool for liquidity providers and one sixth goes to the Injective burn auction, which burns INJ.
The 1% fee traders pay on every buy and sell of a Feast coin.

The 1% fee the Feast hook takes on every buy and sell of a Feast coin, paid in the coin's quote asset (a Binance tokenized stock or BNB). Excludes the PancakeSwap Infinity LP fee and the one-off 1% fee on the FEAST token sale.
The 20% platform share of every fee, plus the self-burn and creator shares of fees in the FEAST/BNB pool, all of which are used to buy and burn the FEAST platform token.
No part of the fee goes to a team treasury: the platform share is used only to buy and burn FEAST.
The rest of each fee, split as the coin's creator fixed it at launch: the creator's share, the referrer's share on referred trades, and the share used to buy back and burn the launched coin itself.
The 20% platform share of every fee, sold by the platform sink for FEAST which is burned, plus the self-burn and creator shares of fees in the FEAST/BNB pool, which buy and burn FEAST.

The 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments, which AI agents make in USDC on Base and Arc for services on Central City's Feed (other payments carry no fee), charged by Central City's immutable fee routers and sent straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.

The full 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments, which AI agents make in USDC on Base and Arc for services on Central City's Feed, kept by Central City: the immutable fee routers send it straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.

The full 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments, which AI agents make in USDC on Base and Arc for services on Central City's Feed, sent by Central City's immutable fee routers straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.
Identical to Fees: every relay fee is paid by the end user out of the amount moved.

Relay fees paid by users on private withdrawals, transfers and holder exits (30 bps plus a fixed gas quote), and the immutable 30 bps service fee on private swaps through the fee route adapters. Ragequit is free.
All Relay fees. Lincoln has no liquidity providers or token holders sharing fees.
Swap service fees are paid to the treasury Safe; relay fees accrue to the protocol-operated relays.

Fees charged when positions settle: a 0.5 basis point close charge on the order value plus the market fee (currently 2%) on the gain of winning trades and on the loss of losing and liquidated trades. Opening a position is free and there are no funding payments.
All settlement fees, split between the protocol and CARDBOARD stakers.
Half of settlement fees, allocated to the protocol fee recipient.
Half of settlement fees, distributed in USDC to CARDBOARD stakers. Referral bonuses are paid from the same budget and are not separated.
2% fee on the profit of every winning trade, taken from the payout. Opening, losing trades and liquidations are free. The house bankroll's trading profit is not counted.
All profit fees, kept by Jupiter. There are no liquidity providers.
All of profit fees, kept by Jupiter. Not used for JUP buybacks.
USDC players pay to open card packs, net of refunds and instant buybacks of won cards, plus marketplace fees on card trades.

Pack sales net of refunds and buybacks, minus payouts to third-party card stakers, referral commissions and draw fees sent to the Jackpot, plus marketplace fees. Payouts for cards staked by the platform's own wallets stay in revenue.
Pack sales net of refunds and buybacks, minus payouts to third-party card stakers, referral commissions and draw fees sent to the Jackpot, plus marketplace fees, all kept by the TopMarket treasury.

Card prices and profit shares paid or credited to third-party stakers whose cards were won, referral commissions settled to referrers, and draw fees routed to the Jackpot prize pool since October 2026.
Swap fees paid by traders, at the dynamic fee the Nami plugin sets for each swap.
Swap fees of gauged pools, paid to Nami token holders: 90% to veNAMI voters and 10% to ogNAMI stakers.
Swap fees paid to Nami fee receivers other than Algebra, veNAMI voters and ogNAMI stakers.
Swap fees of permissionless pools: 99% to liquidity providers and 1% to Algebra as the DEX licence fee.
Swap fees of gauged pools paid to veNAMI voters (90%) and ogNAMI stakers (10%).
Builder fees paid by users on perps trades routed through HypurrTrade (0.05% until 2026-10-08, 0.1% since); excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
Builder fees collected by HypurrTrade from Hyperliquid perps trades.
Users pay each pool's configured fee tier (0.01% to 5%) on every swap.
No protocol fee is taken: the factory owner is burned, so feeProtocol can never be turned on.
All fees: investors pay the management and performance fees, managers (or their trading delegates) pay the trading and vault creation fees.
Management and performance fees paid by vault investors (the manager's and FBYT's parts), plus the SOL trading fee paid on every vault swap and the SOL fee paid to create a vault.
FBYT's share of the management and performance fees, plus all trading and vault creation fees.
The money managers' share of the management and performance fees.

User-paid swap and BNB/WBNB wrapping fees actually credited to WormSwap's fee distributor before protocol allocations, excluding external token transfer taxes, underlying DEX fees, Arena payments and donations.
Net swap and wrapping fee receipts retained by WormSwap and allocated entirely to TANUKI buybacks and burns, with no supplier or referral share.
WormSwap allocates none of its net router fee receipts to a discretionary treasury; all are reserved for TANUKI buybacks and burns.
WormSwap pays no supplier or referral share from its router fee; underlying PancakeSwap liquidity-provider fees belong to PancakeSwap.
Net swap and wrapping fee receipts earmarked for TANUKI buybacks and burns, recognized when received rather than again when the burn batch executes.
The 10% tax traders pay on PSTR buys and sells.

The 10% tax traders pay on PSTR buys and sells, plus the USDC yield earned by the PAPER the treasury has staked on Papertrade, valued at the HYPE it is swapped to and counted when the buyback contract spends it. Tax paid by the buyback contract's own purchases is excluded, since it is paid out of that yield.
All fees: the trade tax goes to the team and the treasury and the yield goes to the team and the buyback.

The trade tax (one tenth to the team, nine tenths to the treasury that acquires and stakes PAPER), the team's 10% share of the staking yield, and the tax the buyback contract pays on its own PSTR purchases.
The staking yield the buyback contract spends buying PSTR and burning it, net of the 10% tax it pays on those purchases.
Taker fees paid by traders on every fill, at 7% x price x (1 - price) per share, minus fees refunded on trades that failed to settle; makers pay no fee.

Taker fees paid by traders whose orders fill against a resting order, at 7% x price x (1 - price) per share, minus fees refunded on trades that failed to settle on Solana; deposit and withdrawal fees are not included.
Taker fees kept by Seeryx after paying 20% back to makers as rebates and refunding fees on trades that failed to settle.
Taker fees kept by Seeryx after maker rebates and refunds, collected into the fee account of the Seeryx program on Solana; Seeryx has no token, so all of it goes to the protocol.
Rebates paid to market makers: 20% of each fill's taker fee goes to the trader whose resting order was filled.
Fees paid by bskts users: the mint fee on buying a basket and the zap-out fee on selling one for USDG, plus each basket's yearly management fee.
All mint, zap-out and management fees, kept by the bskts treasury.
All mint, zap-out and management fees, sent to the bskts treasury.

The 2% fee on every buy and sell of a coin launched on Sapling, the flat fee paid to plant a coin, and Sapling's fee on buys, plantings and sales made from a Zcash account. On Robinhood Chain: the 2% creator tax plus the creator's 70% of Pons's 1% fee on every buy and sell of a coin planted through Sapling, both paid to Sapling's splitter, plus the planting fee and the Zcash account fee, paid in USDG to the treasury. On Raydium LaunchLab (from 2026-10-28): any platform fee claimed from the curve and Sapling's fees from the coin's graduated pool; excludes the coin's transfer tax (Sapling's 2.00% plus the deployer's tax of none to 3%), which is taken on every transfer of the coin, wallet to wallet included.

The part of the 2% coin trading fee Sapling keeps (10% treasury, 25% $SAPLING buyback and burn, 25% $SAPLING/ZEC liquidity), plus the planting fee and the Zcash account fee. For LaunchLab coins, all of the curve platform fee and the graduated pool's fees (a quarter each to the treasury, the flywheel, $SAPLING buyback and burn, and the protocol-owned $SAPLING/ZEC pool). On Robinhood Chain the shares apply to what reaches Sapling's splitter: the 2% creator tax plus the creator's 70% of Pons's 1% fee.

The treasury's share: 10% of the 2% coin trading fee, plus the planting fee and the Zcash account fee. For LaunchLab coins, the treasury's and the flywheel's quarters of the curve platform fee and the graduated pool's fees. On Robinhood Chain the shares apply to what reaches Sapling's splitter: the 2% creator tax plus the creator's 70% of Pons's 1% fee.

40% of the 2% coin trading fee, paid to each coin's deployer, a wallet they choose, or the holders of that coin as holder rewards (on Robinhood Chain, 40% of what reaches Sapling's splitter). LaunchLab coins pay their deployers from the coin's transfer tax, which is not counted.

50% of the 2% coin trading fee: 25% buys and burns $SAPLING, and 25% goes to the $SAPLING/ZEC pool on PumpSwap, where about half of it buys $SAPLING, both sides are deposited and the LP tokens are burned, so no one, Sapling included, can withdraw it. On Robinhood Chain the shares apply to what reaches Sapling's splitter: the 2% creator tax plus the creator's 70% of Pons's 1% fee. For LaunchLab coins, half of the curve platform fee and the graduated pool's fees: $SAPLING buyback and burn, and the protocol-owned $SAPLING/ZEC pool, whose position is locked for good.
Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.
Swap fees kept by fee-earning liquidity providers.
Fees users pay Veil to shield tokens into its private pool, withdraw them, swap privately or fill a private DCA order, plus Veil's share of the relayer fee they pay.

Fees users pay Veil to shield tokens into its private pool, withdraw them, swap privately or fill a private DCA order, plus Veil's share of the relayer fee; network fees, Jupiter's swap fees and tokens swept from closed DCA escrows are not included.
All fees users pay Veil for shielding, withdrawals, private swaps and private DCA fills, plus its share of the relayer fee, all kept by Veil as it has no liquidity providers or stakers to pay.
All fees users pay Veil, collected into the Veil treasury, minus the $VEIL the treasury buys back and burns with 20% of revenue, so it is negative on days when more is burned than earned.
$VEIL bought on the market with 20% of Veil's revenue and burned, counted from the buyback wallet's on-chain burns at the token's price.
Arbitrage profit made through the vaults' pools, as each vault's profit splitter pays it out.
25% of the profit: half to the fee jar, which buys GOO and burns it, and half to the development fund.
12.5% of the profit, paid to the development fund.
75% of the profit, compounded into the vault for its depositors.
12.5% of the profit, sent to the fee jar, which auctions it for GOO and burns the GOO.
Actual builder-code fees paid on Hyperliquid perpetual trades carrying ARX's builder code; excludes Hyperliquid exchange trading fees and legacy ARX builder addresses.
Builder-code fees received by ARX on Hyperliquid perpetual trades, before any subsequent referral payouts from ARX's treasury.
Traders pay the pool's swap fee (EVM) or the launch curve's creator fee (Solana) on every buy and sell.

EVM chains: swap fees of the pools sasa creates for every coin, counted when sasa's builder collects them: the quote-asset side (ETH, BNB or USDC) and the coin side (in the launched coin, valued where the coin has a price). Solana: the creator fees of coins launched on sasa (both halves).
EVM: 70% of the collected swap fees, sent to sasa's fee vault. Solana: sasa's 50% of the creator fees, received by its treasury.
EVM: 30% of the collected swap fees, sent to each coin's creator, or used to buy back and burn the coin when its creator chose buybacks. Solana: the creators' 50% of the creator fees.
Users pay the 0.25% cash-out fee, taken from the amount they cash out.
A 0.25% fee on every cash-out from the Gloam shielded pool. Deposits and private payments are free.
All cash-out fees go to the Gloam fee recipient.
Traders pay the whole swap fee.

The fee the Stockereum hook charges on every swap, in the quote currency, from the hook's Trade event: 1% on v2 launches, 1%, 2% or 3% (chosen by the creator) on v3 launches, plus the anti-snipe rate in the first moments after a launch.
The platform's share of the swap fee: half of the normal 1% on v2, 0.5% of the trade on 1% v3 launches and 1% of the trade on 2% and 3% v3 launches, plus any anti-snipe excess.
The platform's share of the swap fee.
The rest of the swap fee, paid to the launch's creator or, on launches with holder rewards enabled, to the launched token's holders.

Estimated borrowing fees, including supplier flashloan earnings, plus liquidation bonuses and the separately recorded protocol share of flashloan premiums; unpriced collateral bonuses are excluded from USD totals.
Estimated reserve-factor share of borrowing fees, plus the protocol shares of liquidation bonuses and flashloan premiums; unpriced collateral bonuses are excluded from USD totals.
Estimated reserve-factor share of borrowing fees and the protocol shares of liquidation bonuses and flashloan premiums; unpriced collateral bonuses are excluded from USD totals.
Liquidity-index earnings for suppliers, including their flashloan premiums, and liquidation bonuses retained by liquidators; unpriced collateral bonuses are excluded from USD totals.
Users pay the full swap fee charged by the selected V3 pool.
Traders pay the fee tier configured for the pool: 0.01%, 0.05%, 0.30%, or 1%.
Protocol revenue is the exact amount emitted as protocolFeesToken0 or protocolFeesToken1 by each swap.
Protocol revenue accrues in each pool according to its governance-controlled protocol fee.
Liquidity providers receive total swap fees minus the exact protocol-fee amounts emitted by each swap.
Router fee (feeAmount in SherwoodSwap events), charged on the input token.
All router fees go to the TradeWood treasury.

All fees traders pay, before any share goes back to Conviction Pool depositors or referrers: opening and closing fees, liquidation closing fees included, plus the borrowing fees paid while a position is open. Funding is paid between traders and is not counted.
The share of opening and closing fees Nova keeps (governance fee).
The share of opening and closing fees Nova keeps (governance fee). Nova has no token.
The share of opening and closing fees sent to the Conviction Pool (vault, OC, referral and trigger shares) and all borrowing fees.
The 2% fee traders pay on the gain of a profitable perp close; the 2% loss fee is excluded because it is taken from what the LP pool receives, not charged on top of the trader's loss.

2% of the trader's gain on profitable perp closes plus 2% of the margin lost on losing closes and liquidations; the impact haircut on wins and the LP pool's trading profit or loss against traders are not counted.
The 2% fee on profitable perp-close gains and the 2% fee on margin lost in losing closes and liquidations, all kept by the protocol.
Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on trades copied through FiatBear; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
Builder code fees collected by FiatBear on copied trades.
Traders pay the whole trading tax. Launching costs gas only.

The trading tax (1%-5%, set per launch) paid on every curve and graduated-pool trade, in the quote asset. The pools' 0.05% Uniswap v4 LP fee is not included: it is earned by the pool's liquidity and already counted by the Uniswap v4 adapter.
The platform's share of the tax (0.50% of the trade at deployment, frozen into each launch), plus the creator share of launches whose creator wallet is the treasury ($CURB).
The platform's share of the tax on both venues, plus the creator share of treasury-created launches ($CURB), paid to the treasury Safe.
The rest of the tax: to the launch's creator, or to the launch's own token holders through its distributor once holder sharing is on.
Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on perpetual trades placed through Perpex; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
Builder code fees collected by Perpex.

Every swap in a Phlece coin's Uniswap v4 pool pays a 0.98% base fee plus the creator's 1-10% tax, in the coin's paired asset (QuoteFeeTaken events of each coin's hook). Swaps in a coin's first 3 seconds also pay an anti-snipe surcharge. The pool's own LP fee is 0.
20% of every trading fee (the portal's platformBps) plus the whole anti-snipe surcharge go to the Phlece team Safe.
20% of every trading fee plus the anti-snipe surcharge, paid to the Phlece team Safe.

The other 80% of each trading fee, split by percentages the coin's creator fixed at launch between the creator, the coin's holders (dividends), buyback-and-burn of the coin, and liquidity added to the coin's locked pool position.
The open fees and profit fees players pay on settled positions.
